title: Baseline health expenditure conditions paired health and work outcomes
source_unit: MEPS Panel 27 longitudinal person in the civilian noninstitutionalized US population

observations.period: 2022 baseline expenditure band: All valid paired persons

denominator.unit: MEPS Panel 27 persons with valid paired expenditure and perceived-health fields

health_status_improved.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

health_status_worsened.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

out_of_pocket_change.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

out_of_pocket_share_2022.unit: person-level out-of-pocket share of total expenditure, percent
out_of_pocket_share_2022.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

out_of_pocket_share_2023.unit: person-level out-of-pocket share of total expenditure, percent
out_of_pocket_share_2023.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

observations.method: MEPS Panel 27 Longitudinal PUF; baseline 2022 total health expenditure quartiles are weighted cut points among nonnegative expenditure records; paired outcomes use ALL5RDS=1 and their own valid-field universes.
observations.uncertainty: Point estimates use LONGWT. Taylor-linearized standard errors and normal-approximation 95% intervals use LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU. Quartile cells are descriptive and do not adjust for baseline health, age, insurance, income, service mix, or illness severity; expenditure is skewed and quartile cut points are sample-specific.
observations.counterinterpretation: This conditioning pass does not establish that health expenditure caused health or employment change. Baseline expenditure reflects need, prices, coverage, and treatment. The panel does not identify a dated bill, unpaid care hours, schedule control, treatment delay, household debt, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
